incumbent.name: Josh Greene
incumbent.summary: Josh Greene, a Republican and former chief deputy, was chosen sheriff by a Republican caucus in August 2022 after Sheriff Travis Roush stepped down early, and had already won the 2022 Republican primary with no fall opponent; he is not on the 2026 ballot, and no public explanation of his decision was found {wth_greene} {in_list}.
record: August 2022: Republican precinct committee members selected Greene, then chief deputy, to finish Roush's term about five months early; Greene, a 21-year Army veteran who retired from the Indiana Army National Guard as a first sergeant, said he did not plan major changes and did not seek to expand one of the smallest departments in the state {wth_greene}.

January 2025: told the County Council a staffing evaluation recommended 19 jail staff while the jail had nine, and that he believed a few more jail and dispatch staff would make operations safer; commissioners asked the council to explore $5,000 raises for deputies, Greene said Martin County pay was probably $15,000 behind other counties, and the council tabled the raise pending an executive session {mc_council_2025_01_09}.

February 2025: reported hiring a full-time dispatcher, a full-time jailer, part-time dispatchers and jailer, and two full-time deputies, leaving only a part-time cook position open; commissioners approved $4,528 for jail shower-floor repairs {mc_comm_2025_02_18}.

2025: the jail sought out-of-county inmates to offset costs; in January 2025 Greene reported 10 out-of-county inmates against an average in the thirties the prior year {mc_council_2025_01_09}, and at the August 2025 budget meeting the county's financial adviser said $463,000 in out-of-county inmate revenue had been lost and Greene described inconsistent state payments for Department of Correction inmates {mc_budget_2025_08_04}.

2026 budget: the sheriff's general budget was set at $924,620, up from $915,164; Greene said nine deputies including the chief provide patrol coverage and that the 911 system needs replacement as 911 fund revenue declines {mc_budget_2025_08_04}. In September 2025 the council cut the $65,000 patrol-vehicle line to zero, citing financial constraints, and moved two dispatcher positions from the 911 fund to the public safety income tax fund {mc_council_2025_09_29}.

March 2026: Loogootee's police chief and mayor raised delays from split city-county dispatching and proposed a 911 advisory board and possible central dispatch; the sheriff's dispatch commander told commissioners Martin County is the only Indiana county without a computer-aided dispatch (CAD) system {mc_comm_2026_03_17} {mc_comm_2026_03_31}.

race_context: Martin County's sheriff runs a small department and county jail based in Shoals; the department's 2026 staff roster lists a sheriff, chief deputy, nine sworn deputies and jail and dispatch commanders {mc_sheriff_roster}.

This is an open seat: Sheriff Josh Greene is not on the November ballot {in_list}. Both ballot names match senior members of Greene's department on the county roster, Chief Deputy Keith Keller and Capt. Larry Gibson {mc_sheriff_roster}.

Main office issues in 2025–2026 county minutes: deputy and jail staff pay and staffing, lost out-of-county inmate revenue and inconsistent state reimbursements, an aging 911 system and the lack of a CAD system, and split dispatching with Loogootee {mc_council_2025_01_09} {mc_budget_2025_08_04} {mc_comm_2026_03_31}.
May 5, 2026 Republican primary: Keith Keller defeated Jonah Shaw, 1,645 to 468 {sn_primary}.
Larry Gibson is on the ballot as an Independent {in_list}; no coverage of how he qualified was found.
No debate, forum or general-election news coverage of this race was found as of October 11, 2026.

candidates.summary: Keith Keller, the Republican nominee, is chief deputy of the Martin County Sheriff's Office {mc_sheriff_roster} {sn_primary}.
background: Chief deputy under Sheriff Josh Greene, listed on the county's sheriff's office roster {mc_sheriff_roster}; county minutes show him in that role from at least January 2025 {mc_council_2025_01_09}.

Has represented the department before the commissioners: in May 2025 he reported jail population, open deputy and dispatch positions, and costs of the sheriff's mobile app, which commissioners voted 2–1 to reimburse with opioid settlement funds {mc_comm_2025_05_27}; in December 2025 he obtained approval to replace three patrol laptops {mc_comm_2025_12_15}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Jonah Shaw, 1,645 to 468 {sn_primary}.

items: Speaking as chief deputy in March 2026, said dispatchers "do an outstanding job with the equipment they have," that the 911 system needs improvement, and that a CAD system "would be everyone's dream in law enforcement"; he suggested a lower-cost option might be available if bundled with a needed 911 upgrade, recalling an earlier quote of about $400,000 {mc_comm_2026_03_31}.
In May 2025 described the sheriff's mobile app, downloaded by thousands of residents, as an important tool for reaching people who do not use social media {mc_comm_2025_05_27}.

on_incumbent: Is chief deputy to the current sheriff; no campaign statements about Sheriff Greene's record or the office's direction were found.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance totals were found.
gaps: No campaign website, social media platform, interview or candidate questionnaire was found; positions above are statements made as chief deputy at public meetings, not campaign promises.
Years of service, prior ranks and training were not found; older county records reportedly show him as a sergeant around 2015 (search snippet only, unverified).
No positions found on jail staffing, pay, drugs, school resource officers or immigration detainers.
